Academic with a very modern edge
Tatler Schools Guide
The Home of Modern Scholarship
Modern Scholarship is our forward-thinking approach to academic study which is original and relevant to the modern world. It is intellectually thrilling, rooted in the latest research, and designed to nurture academic agility, curiosity and fearless ambition.
Through Modern Scholarship, we support students to take ownership of their learning, think critically and develop the skills and the vision to problem-solve, now and in the future.
The Putney Difference
Everyone’s an original at Putney and creativity isn’t only for artists. Our Faculty for Creative and Visual Arts and Technologies breaks boundaries and celebrates the creativity behind technological entrepreneurship. Musicians compose more than their thoughts and from stage to green screen, everyone has a chance to perform. Editing magazines and software, designing and developing products and apps in the Rapid Prototyping Studio, Putney students are creative trailblazers ready to lead the way in sectors from fashion to fintech to formula one.
Inspired by NASA, Putney High School’s ground-breaking research into benefits of biophilia on wellbeing and academic performance has been adopted by organisations worldwide, as well as earning us a gold medal at the RHS Chelsea Flower Show. Wellbeing and sustainability are at the heart of what we do from our Junior Forest School to our Breathe environmental programme, ensuring every Putney student receives an exceptional education while thoroughly enjoying her childhood. Our proactive, girl-centred care combines with expert teaching and outstanding co-curricular opportunities to promote balance, fun, and resilience, ensuring every pupil feels secure with a strong sense of self and the knowledge they belong.
Co-curricular life at Putney ensures students learn just as much outside the classroom as in it. There is a wealth of opportunity from motorsports to knitting to rowing (from our own boathouse on the Tideway). Whether complete beginner or budding professional, every student has the chance to try something new, develop skills and experience the thrill of pursuing their passions. At Putney, such opportunity is not an add on. We believe it’s fundamental to why our students thrive.
From solving planetary problems with the GDST Space Tech Diploma to creating game-changing apps in Design Thinking and building sustainable start-ups, Putney provides students with the skills and entrepreneurial mindset to ensure they leave us real-world ready. Our Artemis Project gives students space to stretch their intellectual wings and throw themselves into the unknown. An innovative curriculum combined with extensive academic enrichment and award-winning careers support enables students to adapt to an ever-evolving future while ensuring they enjoy their childhood.
We build women of character, consequence and compassion, instilling fearless curiosity, intellectual agility, and a joyful ambition for originality and adventure.
Our Values
We offer a holistic education that focusses on the individual and is outward-looking, encouraging integrity, compassion, respect and social responsibility. We enable every pupil to feel grounded and secure with a strong sense of self and the knowledge that they belong.
Enrichment opportunities are open to all, from inclusive sports clubs to a plethora of music and drama productions throughout the year. Every student can access an enrichment programme designed to help them find their niche.
Forward-thinking in our approach to teaching and learning, we inspire the idea-makers of the future.
Modern scholarship builds our students’ beautiful minds with courses such as Design Thinking offering space for innovation and problem solving. From developing their own apps to improve school life to sharing their expertise in our award-winning publications, students are encouraged to be original thinkers. Little surprise then that Putney alumnae are leading the way around the globe.
Scholarly in our approach to learning, we are creative in our thinking and bold in our ambitions. Our unique blend of Modern Scholarship means learning is intellectually thrilling, rooted in the latest research to build deep, creative thinkers. Each and every girl learns to relish challenge and understand the power of her magnificent mind.
Putney is consistently ranked among the top performing schools in the UK with pupils regularly achieving exceptional outcomes at all levels. Students go on to study at impressive destinations including Oxbridge, UCL and Imperial College, Ivy League universities in the USA, medical schools and leading arts colleges and conservatoires.
Interested and interesting, we are unafraid to stretch our wings and blaze trails, curious to explore and challenge limits.
Putney students learn to be intellectual risk takers, unafraid to make mistakes and learn from them. Through a rich history of debating, our girls learn to be confident communicators. Putney resilient, creative thinkers with entrepreneurial spirits ready to carve the way in innovative and varied careers.
Girls are given the confidence to be who they want to be

pageCache.pageTitle: Staff, Governors & Trustees ⋆ Putney High School London GDST
pageCache.text:
Staff, Governors & Trustees
Putney has a culture of inspiration, innovation, energy and creativity in teaching, and this character shapes the learning of our pupils.
From our Head, Jo Sharrock, to the many scholars, published authors, skilled artists, composers, playwrights and Olympian sports coaches; every one plays a part in creating the stimulating learning environment for which Putney is known. It makes our school an innovative, dynamic and really exciting place to teach, and above all, to learn.
Jo Sharrock – Head
Jo Sharrock joined Putney High School GDST in September 2023 following a five year headship at Shrewsbury High School and previous role as Deputy Head Pastoral at Queen Elizabeth’s Hospital School in Bristol.
An innovative, caring and dynamic leader, Ms Sharrock is deeply committed to helping every student fulfil their potential – whether that is through academic studies, co-curricular interests or building strength of character.
Ms Sharrock graduated with first class honours in History from the University of Leeds and worked in the finance industry for organisations including Goldman Sachs, NatWest and HSBC before deciding to pursue a career in teaching. She completed her PGCE at the University of the West of England.
Ms Sharrock credits her professional success to her own all-girls education. She very much shares Putney’s passion for forward-thinking excellence and typifies the school’s down to earth, warm approach that inspires each and every student to be curious, creative and bold.
Senior School
Phoebe Bradley – Deputy Head Academic
Mrs Phoebe Bradley joined Putney High School in September 2015 as Head of History & Politics. She joined the SLT in 2018 as Director of Pupil Progress & Academic Enrichment before taking on the role of Deputy Head Academic in 2020. She job shares the role with Pippa Gilbert.
Mrs Bradley obtained a degree in History from New College, Oxford, specialising in the history of the scientific revolution. Having returned to Oxford University to obtain her PGCE in 2012; she previously taught at Rochester Grammar School.
Together with Mrs Gilbert, Mrs Bradley is committed to promoting an ethos of modern scholarship – ensuring learning at Putney is an exciting, joyous journey of discovery. Throughout their time leading the Academic SLT, both have promoted a culture of research-led practice, most notably in their development of the school’s renowned Science of Learning curriculum – which ensures both staff and students understand the neuroscience behind how learning happens, thus enabling students to maximise their enormous cognitive potential.
Pippa Gilbert – Deputy Head Academic
Mrs Pippa Gilbert joined Putney High School in September 2015 as a Religious Studies teacher. She joined the SLT in 2018 as Director of Research, Learning & Outreach, having been the Gifted & Talented Coordinator, and became Deputy Head Teaching & Learning in 2020 before taking on the role of Deputy Head Academic in 2022. She job shares the roles with Phoebe Bradley.
Mrs Gilbert has earned national renown for the quality of her teaching, as a finalist and silver award winner at the Pearson National Teaching Awards in 2019. She championed the introduction, and now thriving culture, of action research within the school, and has presented at the Festival of Education as well as being an award-winner within the GDST for her research on Harkness tables.
Together with Mrs Bradley, Mrs Gilbert is committed to promoting an ethos of modern scholarship – ensuring learning at Putney is an exciting, joyous journey of discovery. Throughout their time leading the Academic SLT, both have promoted a culture of research-led practice, most notably in their development of the school’s renowned Science of Learning curriculum.
Jane Brandon – Deputy Head Pastoral & Co-curricular
Dr Brandon is passionate about offering pupils opportunities to take part in a vibrant co-curricular programme along with volunteering and partnerships that develops independence, kindness and reflects and embodies the school’s ‘It Starts With Me’ pastoral ethos.
Dr Brandon’s first degree is from King’s College London, where she studied Musicology. She continued her musical studies there, leading to the completion of her PhD in 2008. She went on to gain a PGCE in Secondary Music from the Institute of Education, while combining her studies with offering free music tuition as part of a community music project. She began her teaching career as head of Academic Music at St Mary’s Ascot, quickly progressing to the role of Assistant Head of Sixth Form.
James Mutton – Deputy Head Curriculum & Digital Innovation
Mr James Mutton (MA Hons Geography (Edinburgh), MEd Cambridge) studied Geography at Edinburgh where he decided to become a teacher after spending much of his time volunteering with young people alongside studying. After a year as an Assistant House Master in the Junior School at Gordonstoun, he completed a PGCE at the Faculty of Education in Cambridge and moved to London where he has taught ever since. Ever keen to combine academic study with school life, he has recently earned a third Masters, this time in Educational Leadership and Management from the University of Roehampton.
James has a wide-ranging portfolio of whole school responsibilities which include managing the Senior School timetable, developing a forward-looking curriculum and leading on digital innovation. Most recently this has included adopting Python as one of our language options in Year 9 to allow students to develop their coding skills, ready for their digital future. He is determined to ensure that Putney students leave with the skills, resilience and confidence they need to be trailblazers in their chosen paths.
Conor Johnston – Director of Sixth Form
Mr Conor Johnston joined Putney High School in 2026 to lead the Sixth Form team.
Mr Johnston joined Putney following a period at Woldingham School as Head of Economics. He brings extensive Sixth Form leadership experience as he was previously Director of Sixth Form at Sir William Perkins’s School, and the Assistant Director of Sixth Form at Surbiton High School.
Mr Johnston completed his PGCE at Swansea Metropolitan University and holds a Bachelors degree in Economics & Classical Civilisation from National University College Galway and a Masters in Education from Middlesex University.
Junior School
Liz McLaughlin – Junior School Head
Harvard-educated Ms Liz McLaughlin brings with her more than a decade’s experience of Headship. She joins us from Wetherby School, Kensington and was previously Head at Falcons Pre-Prep School, Chiswick, and before that, Primary School Principal at the International School of London. A passionate advocate for single sex education, she is a visionary who shares Putney’s commitment to research and the science of learning. Her own research interests have centred on curriculum development and literacy.
Ella Wilson – Deputy Head Academic
Ms Wilson joined Putney High Junior School in 2026 as Deputy Head Academic.
Previously Assistant Head Academic at Garden House School, Ms Wilson brings with her a wealth of knowledge and expertise within London day schools and in particular, girls’ education through her role as Head of Mathematics at Bute House Prep.
She is passionate about inspiring pupils and staff through innovative teaching and learning, enabling children to harness their natural curiosity and reach their potential.
Ms Wilson studied Biological Sciences with Medical Biology at the University of Edinburgh, before completing her Primary PGCE at London South Bank University. She has taught in the state and independent sector in London and internationally.
Isobel Franks – Deputy Head Pastoral
Miss Isobel Franks joined Putney High Junior School in January 2012, first as a Year 5 Class Teacher, then as Pastoral Tutor and Key Stage 2 Coordinator. She has been Deputy Head Pastoral since September 2017. Miss Franks has a particular interest in wellbeing and the social and emotional aspects of learning. She oversees the Opening Minds programme in the Junior School, which aims to enable pupils to develop a deeper understanding of themselves, of others and of their place in the world.
Miss Franks is a trained Pawsb mindfulness teacher, and she is an accredited member of the Positive Schools Programme. She was an early adopter of our coaching programme, contributing to the collaborative culture that exists here at Putney. She has recently begun training in Child Counselling with Place2Be.
Miss Franks has visited schools in Pakistan and India, working alongside local teachers to share best practice and innovative ideas.
In her spare time, Miss Franks enjoys dressmaking and growing fruit and vegetables on her allotment.

The Co-Chairs of the Trustees, Stuart Ross and Ann Ewing, can be contacted via Ms Lucy Colegate (GDST Head of Governance) at the GDST office.

pageCache.pageTitle: Partnerships ⋆ Putney High School London GDST
pageCache.text:
Partnerships
Our pupils take part in mentoring programmes, collaborate with future industry leaders, and even enjoy bushcraft activities on Wimbledon Common. We create inclusive opportunities for pupils of all ages to get involved, learn from others, and make a meaningful impact.
Working Together
Throughout the year, our staff and students work closely with local schools, universities and other organisations on practical projects, research and partnerships that benefit the wider community, support charitable causes and enhance the curriculum.
West London Schools Partnership
We are proud to be a founding member of the West London Partnership – an initiative uniting secondary schools from both the independent and state sectors across West and South West London. Through collaboration, we create exciting opportunities for pupils to learn from one another, share ideas and develop skills together – from entrepreneurship challenges and Model UN debates to visits from influential figures including the US Ambassador to career forums to name just some.
Future Medics Programme
Generously funded by HSBC Bank and run in partnership with our West London Partnership network, this initiative supports Year 12 pupils aiming for a career in medicine. Through expert guidance from UCAS to interview preparation and the UCAT, students develop the confidence and skills they need to apply successfully to leading medical schools.
Festival of Sport
Our annual Festival of Sport brings together more than 150 local primary school children to try new sports, develop skills and build friendships before they move on to senior school. Pupils from Putney High School and St Cecilia’s Secondary School take on leadership roles, supporting a range of engaging team building and sporting activities.

House Charities
Every year, each of our four Houses chooses a charity as the focus of their fundraising activities.

2026 ISI Inspection
In April 2026, a team of eight ISI inspectors visited Putney High School. As a result of this inspection, we are delighted that Putney has been awarded a significant strength for our ethos of Modern Scholarship.
“Pupils develop self-confidence in their decision-making.”
Our significant strength
Inspectors found our approach of ‘Modern Scholarship’ to teaching and learning is a significant strength. This is a rare accolade which recognises a provision judged to be outstanding in the sector.
The report from April 2026 states,
“Leaders provide an aspirational curriculum that helps to prepare pupils for the future. They promote the concept of ‘Modern Scholarship’ which fosters a spirit of enquiry. Pupils across the school are curious and motivated to learn.”
“Pupils are highly ambitious and motivated to achieve well. They apply intellectual, physical and creative effort in a range of opportunities available to them. This is a significant strength of the school.”
Key Findings
Pupils learn about the ‘science of learning’ to develop an understanding of how they learn and an awareness of their own progress.

pageCache.pageTitle: Results & Destinations ⋆ Putney High School GDST
pageCache.text:
With nine applications for every place, parents clearly rate the academic prowess of Putney High.
Tatler Schools Guide
Exceptional Results
Putney High School is consistently ranked among the top performing schools both in London and the UK with pupils regularly achieving exceptional outcomes at 11+, GCSE and A Level.
Students go on to pursue a broad range of interests at impressive destinations in the UK and abroad, including at the universities of Oxford and Cambridge, UCL and Imperial College, Ivy League universities in the USA, medical schools and leading arts colleges and conservatoires.
Leavers’ Destinations

What if learning looked different?
The Artemis Project is a dedicated space in the school week for originality and adventure, time given over to revelling in academic exploration. Artemis blurs subject boundaries, encourages big questions, invention and original thinking.
Named after the goddess Artemis, the project, like NASA’s own, seeks to grow a new generation of explorers – whether interstellar or thoroughly terrestrial – giving students space to stretch their intellectual wings and to throw themselves into the unknown.
Through Artemis we take on the adventure of intellectual discovery, revelling in the thrill of complex problem solving and deepening our ability to critique, create, collaborate and innovate.
The seven Artemis competencies
Performance Whether under stage lights or open skies, sing, tell stories, or pluck strings in musical and dramatic productions inspired by everything from ancient Greece to the Earthshot Prize.
Data and Digital What is data? How can it help us to understand the world and how can we collect it ethically? Become a detective through exploration of real-world data and discover the foundations of data intelligence and digital fluency.
Wellbeing Strong in mind and body. Learn self-defence and self-regulation as you develop a personal mindfulness routine and a sense of awareness for potentially dangerous situations.
Leadership Dissect the role of leadership in sports as we put rowing under the microscope at our boathouse. Harness the science of performance to set goals, motivate, and lead.
Maths in Art Explore the fascinating intersection of mathematics and art as you calculate the mathematical underpinnings of artistic beauty. Ponder patterns and pursue the creation of your own portfolio piece.
Putney Publishing House Can you be as quirky as Quentin Blake? Might you match the mastery of Michael Rosen? Move from imagination to page to bookshelf, learning about the challenges of the publishing world.
Game Theory From competition and cooperation to risk and reward, explore the mathematics of decision-making, strategy and human behaviour. Collaborate, debate and think critically as you justify decisions and predict outcomes.
Putney Debates The grown-ups who dominate decision-making are rotten reasoners and even worse wordsmiths. Develop the skills to create logical and articulate arguments. Politicians may brag, blague and bluster, but Putney debates!
The Psychology of Leadership Discover the trophy winning mindset of high performing teams and learn to lead the way, your way. Improve your decision making and communication and uncover what you bring to the table.
Adventurous Training Can you cook on a campfire and find your way in the forest? Unlock adventure with expedition training built on core survival principles: shelter, nutrition, navigation, first aid.
Community Partnerships Create positive impact through meaningful volunteering experiences. Through service, develop ethical and inclusive citizenship, empathy, responsibility and confidence.
International Perspectives Whether your tastebuds tingle with the food of the Mandarin diaspora or your eyes light up with the cinematic storytelling of the frères lumière, channel your Putney intrepidity.
Classical London How has London’s identity been forged by settlement, migration, belief and power? Dive into history, mythology and more as you connect Londinium to the London of today and tomorrow.
Make a Million Take on the stock market, harnessing creativity and innovation to design bold marketing strategies and challenging yourself to turn a small seed fund into a profitable venture.
Psychology From Freud to King’s College, turn back time to explore our evolving understanding of mental health, drawing on London’s status as a historical hub for psychological thought.
Statues, Faith, Democracy Immerse yourself in the hidden narratives of those who shaped our city and uncover the stories behind our statues from the British Museum to Parliament Square.
Pain and Pills Experiment, innovate, iterate and analyse as you conduct a practical exploration of the process of pain management, the synthesis of pain killers and the psychological effects of pain.
Made in Putney Dig deeper into Putney from its role in the development of British democracy to its strategic position on the Thames as you research, film and edit your own Putney film production.
Artemis: A Level above
Build digital fluency, flex your creative design muscles, go global and go beyond your A Levels at Putney High School Sixth Form. From prototyping ideas to pitching digital businesses, Artemis builds the skills, experience and confidence to distinguish yourself at university and in future careers.
Design, build and pitch your own creative digital business idea, harnessing Design Thinking, agile project management, entrepreneurship and practical digital product development.
Define problems, prototype ideas, and adapt to challenges throughout a creative design project guided by expert practitioners. You will set extended timelines, make independent decisions and develop resilience.
Enhance your cognitive and problem-solving skills and develop your cultural awareness in an increasingly interconnected world. Investigate language and culture. Revel in literature architecture and film.
Year 13 Leadership Programme: Creating Tomorrow’s Leaders
What is leadership? How can we lead ethically? How can we work together to deliver impact?
Gain the skills, experience, and confidence to lead. Through specialist coaching, develop the skills you need to plan and deliver an academic event, publication, outreach initiative or community project.
Leave Putney a leader with the initiative, organisational skills, and resilience you need to make an impact.
Unashamedly unexamined, the Project, like the goddess herself, is about freedom – freedom to break down traditional disciplinary boundaries, freedom to think differently, freedom to learn differently, freedom to explore the unexpected.
Phoebe Bradley, Deputy Head Academic

Senior School Bursaries
A number of means-tested bursaries are available for pupils entering Year 7 or Year 12.
From full bursaries – which include fees, uniform and other extras to allow your daughter to be a part of everything that a Putney (GDST) education offers – through to smaller, tailored financial assistance packages, we are keen to support as many girls as possible.
There may be strong competition for bursaries, and they are therefore awarded on the basis of financial eligibility and academic potential – that is, high achievement in the 11+ entrance assessment for Year 7 entry, or 16+ assessments and GCSE results for Sixth Form entry. We want girls who show academic merit and potential to join our school.

Please note the deadline for bursary applications is the same day as the application for the school.

If the applicant is awarded a bursary, it is expected that this will remain throughout their time at Putney High School from when they join us to the completion of their A-level studies in Year 13. The value of the award will be reviewed by the GDST annually around April and is dependent on continuing good progress and conduct.
Bursary FAQs
The key difference is that a bursary is means-tested and a scholarship isn’t. We offer bursaries so that a GDST education is accessible to the best and the brightest girls, including those who are not in a position to pay full fees.
A bursary takes into account academic ability but its value is directly related to the income and financial resources of the pupil’s family.
Scholarships are awarded purely on academic (or sporting or musical) merit, as measured in a competitive entrance exam, and take no account of family income or resources.
Many of our bursaries and scholarships are funded via charitable partnerships and by donations and legacies from our former pupils, their parents, and other friends.
To assess who is eligible for a bursary we consider a range of objective criteria including the income and capital resources of the families applying.
A family’s residency status also determines eligibility. At the time of application both the child and parent are required to have one of the following: a British passport, Indefinite Leave to Remain or Settled status through the EU Settlement Scheme.
Your child’s academic performance will be a key consideration when the school is deciding whether or not to award a bursary.
It is anticipated that bursary awards will last for the duration of the student’s time at school. We re-assess every year to take account of changes in family income and circumstances. A bursary may go up or down to reflect these. This ensures those most in need receive our support.
Bursaries range from 30% to 100% of fees; however, the amount of any bursary also depends on the funding available. Sometimes awards of a lesser value may be offered. Pupils who get a full bursary may also get help to meet the cost of their uniforms, lunches and travel.
The values of scholarships vary, but are generally small and more about the honour of the award than the amount given. A scholarship may, however, be supplemented by a bursary.
